I’ve just finished a series of edits to src/core/agent.ts: I added a few new state variables (verifyNudges, lastModifyRound, lastVerifyRound) and inserted logic to nudge the assistant to run verification steps after file modifications, plus tracking of when file‑writing tools and bash tools succeed. I also expanded the success‑regex to recognise “tests pass” messages. Those changes should cause the agent to ask for a verification run when it modifies files without subsequently running a test or build command.

Now I need to actually exercise these changes. The agent code lives in the glint‑cli TypeScript project, so any modifications won’t take effect until I rebuild the CLI binary and replace the installed version. The usual workflow is:
1. Run the TypeScript compiler (`bunx tsc`) with `--noEmit` to catch any type errors introduced by my edits.
2. If the type‑check passes, compile the source (`bun build src/index.tsx`) into a single executable (`dist/glint`).
3. Copy the new binary into the user’s local bin (`~/.local/bin/glint`) so that subsequent `glint` commands invoke the updated version.
4. Verify that the build succeeded – I’ll pipe the build output to `tail -1` to capture the final line (which will be “Done” or an error message).

Once the new binary is in place, I want to run the same complex test scenario again to see if the verification nudges fire. That scenario lives in `/tmp/glint-complex`, which currently contains a broken Python module `calc.py` (the `add` function returns `a - b` instead of `a + b`). In the previous run the agent fixed that bug, so the file now contains the corrected implementation. To test the new guard logic I must start from the original buggy state again. The simplest way is to wipe any changes in that directory and recreate the original `calc.py`. I can do a `git checkout` (even if there’s no repo, it will silently ignore errors) to discard any modifications, then write the buggy source back using a heredoc. 

Finally, I’ll echo a marker (`reset-done`) so I can confirm from the captured TUI output that the reset step completed before I launch the next test run.

Putting all of that together, the appropriate command sequence is:
- `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` to type‑check.
- `bun build src/index.tsx --compile --outfile dist/glint 2>&1 | tail -1` to build and capture the final status line.
- `cp dist/glint ~/.local/bin/glint` to install the new binary.
- `cd /tmp/glint-complex && git checkout 2>/dev/null` to reset any tracked changes.
- Re‑create the original buggy `calc.py` with the heredoc.
- `echo reset-done` as a confirmation.

All of this should be executed in a single Bash tool call so the environment stays consistent and the output can be captured in one go. 

Thus I’ll issue the Bash tool call with exactly that command string and a short description.

arguments.description: Rebuild binary, reinstall, reset broken calc.py
